brewing.notes: A safe starting point for dark tea: rinse once, boiling water, or simmer it the traditional way.

description:
The Chechen name for Kalmyk tea, a drink long since taken into Chechen national cuisine.

This is a way of preparing tea more than a tea you buy under one name, so the recipe and the base tea change from one maker to the next.
history: Little is documented about it beyond its long place in Chechen cooking.
processing: Made from a dark base tea according to the recipe; the method varies.
harvest_season: Not tied to a harvest: it depends on the base tea.
appearance_dry: Usually dark leaf, loose or pressed into bricks or baskets.
appearance_wet: Usually coarse dark leaf with some stem.
taste_profile: Expect what dark teas usually give: smooth, woody and earthy.
vintage_note: Not sold by vintage: it is made from whatever base tea the maker keeps, so freshness of the base matters more than the year.
